subsystems.name: Decentralized Identifier (DID) layer
subsystems.role: gives each user and organisation a unique, self-owned identifier that resolves to cryptographic public keys.

subsystems.name: Verifiable Credential (VC) layer
subsystems.role: digitally signed claims about a subject that can be checked without contacting the issuer.

subsystems.name: Wallet
subsystems.role: user-controlled app that stores DIDs, credentials and private keys, and presents proofs.

subsystems.name: Trust registry / ledger
subsystems.role: provides a tamper-evident record for DIDs, schemas and revocation lists.

subsystems.name: Governance framework
subsystems.role: defines the rules, schemas and legal recognition that make credentials trustworthy.

buildSteps.title: Define governance and schemas
buildSteps.detail: Stakeholders agree on credential types, data fields, privacy rules and who can issue what.

buildSteps.title: Choose DID method and ledger
buildSteps.detail: Select how DIDs are created and resolved, and whether a public or private ledger anchors trust.

buildSteps.title: Develop issuer software
buildSteps.detail: Build the service that creates and signs verifiable credentials using the issuer’s private key.

buildSteps.title: Develop wallet
buildSteps.detail: Create the user app that generates keys, requests credentials and stores them securely on a phone or computer.

buildSteps.title: Develop verifier software
buildSteps.detail: Build the component that requests a proof, checks the signature and validates the issuer’s trust status.

buildSteps.title: Issue credentials
buildSteps.detail: An issuer signs a credential and sends it to the holder’s wallet, often after an identity check.

buildSteps.title: Verify and present
buildSteps.detail: The holder selects which credentials to share; the verifier cryptographically checks them without calling the issuer.

buildSteps.title: Handle revocation and rotation
buildSteps.detail: Publish revocation lists or status endpoints so expired or compromised credentials can be rejected.

prerequisites.tech: Public key cryptography and digital signatures
prerequisites.why: credentials are only trustworthy if they are signed and can be verified offline.
provides a decentralised, tamper-evident anchor for DIDs and schemas without a central authority.

prerequisites.tech: W3C standards for DIDs and Verifiable Credentials
prerequisites.why: ensure different wallets and issuers can interoperate.
enable selective disclosure (e.g., proving age without revealing birthdate), but are not yet widespread.
revoking credentials at scale without tracking users remains a research and engineering challenge.

pathway.milestone: government and enterprise pilots (e.g., EU Digital Identity Wallet, travel credentials)
pathway.unlocks: real-world testing of wallets, issuers and verifiers.

pathway.milestone: interoperable wallets across borders and sectors
pathway.unlocks: credentials issued in one country recognised in another.

pathway.milestone: integration with national digital identity schemes
pathway.unlocks: citizens using SSI alongside or instead of traditional logins for public services.

pathway.milestone: mainstream adoption for civic services, replacing passwords and physical documents
pathway.unlocks: user-controlled identity that reduces data breaches and simplifies access to services.
